reference_answers: The main objective is to apply deep learning — specifically Artificial Neural Networks — to a finite element study set up using a Design of Experiments framework for a steering knuckle, enabling prediction of stress, strain, and displacement, and identifying optimal design parameters via an Inverse Prediction Algorithm.
The output parameters are maximum von Mises stress, maximum displacement, and maximum strain.
A dataset comprising 6000 unique design points was generated using the Latin Hypercube DoE method via Simulia Isight and Abaqus.

Latin Hypercube Sampling (LHS) was used because it provides efficient coverage of the entire design space with far fewer simulations than a full factorial approach, ensuring at least one data point per interval for each variable, which benefits neural network training.

The Full Factorial method was abandoned because it was computationally expensive and time-consuming — it required an extremely large number of simulations when handling 8 load parameters, 6 geometric parameters, and 1 material property across multiple levels.
Simulia Isight was used as the central design optimization and automation platform, governing Abaqus CAE, which performed the structural finite element analysis for each design iteration.
The 15 parameters are 8 load variables (X1–X8), 6 geometric design variables (X9–X14, namely fillet radii R1–R5 and tie rod arm thickness L1), and 1 material property — Young's modulus (X15).
A 5mm mesh size was used in the Abaqus CAE-based finite element model to ensure converged results.

The neural network has an input layer with 15 neurons, multiple hidden layers with 64, 32, and 16 neurons respectively using ReLU activation, and an output layer with a single neuron predicting the continuous target variable (stress, strain, or displacement).
ReLU (Rectified Linear Unit) activation functions were used in the hidden layers to introduce non-linearity and mitigate the vanishing gradient problem.
Adam (Adaptive Moment Estimation) optimization algorithm was used to minimize the Mean Squared Error (MSE) loss function during training.
An Early Stopping callback was employed during training, which monitored validation loss and terminated training if the validation loss did not improve for a predefined number of epochs.
The overall accuracy achieved by the neural network model across all three target variables is 97.103%.

The Inverse Prediction Algorithm uses the pre-trained neural network to identify the optimal combination of geometric design parameters that minimizes stress, strain, and displacement for a given set of loading conditions. It creates a refined full factorial design and systematically evaluates each combination using the pre-trained model.
The accuracy achieved for strain is 96%, for stress is 97.86%, and for displacement is 97.45%.
The four loading conditions considered are acceleration (0.5g), braking (1.1G), bump load (2.5G at lower suspension, 1.1G at upper suspension), and cornering (1.2g lateral acceleration).

Simulia Isight acts as the central design optimization platform, defining design variables, specifying the DoE method (LHS), automating the Abaqus solver, and collecting the resulting stress, strain, and displacement outputs for all 6000 design points.

The six geometric design variables are: fillet radius between lower and upper suspension arms (R1, R2), fillet radius at the junction between tie rod arm and hub (R3), fillet radius at the junction between hub and upper suspension strut mounting point (R4), oblique junction between upper suspension strut mounting and hub (R5), and thickness of the tie rod mounting arm (L1).
Young's modulus, which is a measure of material stiffness, was the sole material property parametrized alongside the geometric and load variables.

The authors suggest extending the framework to thermal analysis (transient thermal analysis of brake disc rotor) and dynamic scenarios (vibration of a clamped plate), as well as combining the approach with generative design and topology optimization for benchmarking and further design optimization.
